parole.testo: Partial calque from Chinese 樟茶鴨／樟茶鸭 (zhāngcháyā, “camphor-tea duck”).

parole.significato: A poisonous bird from Chinese mythology that is said to have existed in what is now southern China.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Chinese 鴆鳥 /鸩鸟 (zhènniǎo)

parole.significato: Expressing distress, regret, or fear.
parole.testo: Mainly borrowed from Tamil ஐயோ (aiyō) and Sinhalese අයියෝ (ayiyō). Common in Dravidian languages; compare Telugu అయ్యో (ayyō), Kannada ಅಯ್ಯೋ (ayyō), Malayalam അയ്യോ (ayyō), Tulu ಅಯ್ಯೋ (ayyō), Kurux अयो (ayo). Alternatively from Chinese 哎喲 /哎哟 (āiyō) in Malaysia and Singapore.

parole.significato: A member of an ancient Central Asian tribe; later, a member of the ruling dynasty and people of the Kushan Empire.
